Project Name: Digital Bio-Shield

Digital Bio-Shield is an AI-powered health monitoring and protection system designed to safeguard astronauts during long-duration space missions, particularly journeys to Mars. It addresses the major health risks of space travel, including radiation exposure, bone deterioration, microgravity, and delayed communication with Earth.

The system combines Edge AI with a Bio-Twin (Digital Biological Twin) to create a personalized digital model of each astronaut's body. Using biological data inspired by NASA GeneLab, it continuously monitors health indicators and predicts potential cellular damage before visible symptoms appear. When a health risk is detected, the AI analyzes the situation, alerts the astronaut, and provides immediate recommendations without depending on communication with Earth.

Digital Bio-Shield also supports adaptive environmental adjustments, including radiation protection and sleep simulation, to help maintain astronauts' physical well-being.

Our project's importance lies in shifting space healthcare from reactive treatment to proactive prevention, making long-duration human space exploration safer, smarter, and more sustainable.https://drive.google.com/file/d/1n3BJKFNQmzDFiG5J2MzLz8dVsJidNMt2/view?usp=drivesdk
details: Digital Bio-Shield – The Digital Biological Shield Digital Bio-Shield is an intelligent system that uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) to monitor astronauts' health and predict potential health risks before symptoms appear, especially during long-duration space missions to Mars. The project works by creating a Digital Bio-Twin of the human body, which analyzes biological data and monitors changes caused by radiation exposure and microgravity. It also uses Edge AI technology to process data inside the spacecraft without requiring a continuous connection to Earth. The project relies on Artificial Intelligence, data analysis, and biological databases such as NASA GeneLab to detect health risks early, send alerts to the medical team, and provide recommendations that support medical decision-making. The creative aspect of the project is that it does not simply monitor astronauts' health; it predicts potential health problems before they occur. This can help protect astronauts and improve their safety during long-duration space missions.
